text:
Alex Chen: Heads up — on the latency dashboard for /v2/generate the p95 line is consistently above p99 for the canary slice. UI bug or math error?
Priya Nair: whoa. can you paste the endpoint + time window?
Alex Chen: /v2/generate, canary=true, last 6h. screenshot attached (but tl;dr p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 380ms).
Omar Velasquez: odd. p95 > p99 can't happen if both are computed from same raw distribution. likely aggregation/merge ordering.
Dana Brooks: the canary traffic is routed through fallback pools sometimes — weights change mid-window. that can change per-bucket counts.
Priya Nair: we recently switched the console to do per-minute tdigest merges and then show percentiles from the merged tdigest. if buckets have different client tags, merge order can bias pctl.
Alex Chen: is there a quick query I can run to show raw values?
Omar Velasquez: try this (internal metrics DSL):
```
metrics.query(
  metric="latency_ms",
  filter=["endpoint:/v2/generate","canary:true"],
  aggregator="raw_samples",
  window="6h"
)
```
Priya Nair: if you pull raw_samples you'll see the p99 > p95 as expected. the dashboard path is: fetch per-minute tdigest -> merge -> compute percentiles. the merge is not stable if we weight by sample counts that changed.
Dana Brooks: to be precise: we do tdigest per-shard, compress, then merge. if counts are low for the tail buckets and a later heavy-minute bucket has shorter tails (cold starts filtered differently), the merged shape can flip.
Alex Chen: ok so UX is lying to engineers. can we show provenance (merge mode + sample counts) on the tooltip?
Priya Nair: yes — we already have sample_count per-minute. minimal UX change: add a small badge "merge=minute-tdigest, samples=XX" in the hover.
Omar Velasquez: long-term fix: compute percentiles from the concatenated raw stream (or use streaming merge mode that preserves tail mass) before downsampling. but that can be expensive on high-throughput endpoints.
Dana Brooks: and note: routing policy changes (fallback weights) during a rollout will shift sample origin. telemetry already tags requests with route_weight and sample_origin but console doesn't surface origin by default.
Alex Chen: could the quota fallback cause this? e.g., when quota exhausted we route to cheaper model with different latency distribution.
Priya Nair: yup. quota-triggered fallback is a route-level tag. when a client hits quota the route tag becomes `fallback_quota=true`. downstream tdigest buckets then represent mixed distributions.
Alex Chen: action items?
Priya Nair: 1) small UX: show merge mode + per-slice sample_count in tooltip. 2) short-term backend: add an option toggle "compute pctl from raw samples when sample_count < threshold". 3) long-term: implement stable tdigest merge or switch to q-digest for rollup.
Omar Velasquez: I'll prototype a server-side flag `percentile_compute_mode=raw_if_sparse` and test on /v2/generate canary.
Dana Brooks: I'll file a console PR to surface `sample_origin` and `merge_mode` in the hover and legend.
metrics-bot: Note: new metric tag `sample_origin` available on metric ingestion starting 1717480000.
deploy-bot: canary updated: routing policy tweak deployed to us-west-2 (revision r582). :rocket:
Alex Chen: thanks. Omar — ping me when you have the prototype, will run SLO gating check.
Priya Nair: one more thought — we should add a small explain text under percentile chart: "Percentiles computed from merged per-minute histograms by default; toggle to raw-sample mode for low-volume slices." saves time.
Dana Brooks: agree. small UX + backend flag covers 90%.
Alex Chen: great. I'll update the rollout checklist to include "check percentile provenance" before next canary. :white_check_mark:
